data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise article use with general and specific nouns, geographical names, institutions and common proper names.
data.learningTitle: Using Articles with Nouns and Names
learningPoints: Use a/an for one non-specific singular countable noun.
Use the for specific or unique nouns.
Use zero article for many proper names, languages and general plural nouns.
Use the with some geographical names such as rivers, seas and mountain ranges.
Recognise common institutional expressions such as go to school or be in hospital.
Distinguish general meaning from specific reference.

sections.summary: Using zero article with a country name.
sections.explain: Most country names take no article.

words.word: She lives in France.
She lives in the France.
She lives in a France.
The Thames runs through London.
Thames runs through London.
A Thames runs through London.
They went skiing in the Alps.
They went skiing in Alps.
They went skiing in an Alps.

sections.summary: Using zero article with a city name.
sections.explain: Most city names take no article.

words.word: Madrid is the capital of Spain.
The Madrid is the capital of Spain.
A Madrid is the capital of Spain.

sections.explain: Use THE when both speaker and listener know which noun is meant.

words.word: Could you close the window, please?
Could you close a window, please, the one beside you?
Could you close window, please?

sections.summary: Using zero article for general plural nouns.
sections.explain: Plural nouns take no article when speaking generally.

words.word: Computers are useful tools.
The computers are useful tools in general.
A computers are useful tools.

sections.explain: Use A/AN when mentioning one non-specific singular countable noun for the first time.

words.word: I saw a man outside the station.
I saw the man outside the station for the first time, any man.
I saw man outside the station.

sections.explain: After introducing something with A/AN, use THE for the same thing.

words.word: I bought a book. The book was very interesting.
I bought the book. A book was very interesting.
I bought a book. Book was very interesting.

sections.summary: Using zero article in an institutional expression.
sections.explain: Use no article with SCHOOL when referring to its normal function.

words.word: My children are at school now.
My children are at the school now, meaning they are pupils there.
My children are at a school now, as a fixed expression.

sections.explain: Names of seas normally take THE.

words.word: They sailed across the Mediterranean.
They sailed across Mediterranean.
They sailed across a Mediterranean.
